original:
Jesus, your parable in Matthew 13:47 lays a net across the whole sea and pulls up everything — the edible and the inedible together. I sit with it longer than I want to. The net is your work, not mine. The sorting is also your work. My duty is the haul, not the verdict. I keep being tempted to start the sorting early, to anticipate the angels' job and rule on which of my neighbours belongs in which pile. It is bad theology and worse manners. Forgive the way I have run a private hell in my own head and posted the verdicts. The fish that look unappetizing to me are not necessarily the ones the Lord of the catch will discard. The fish that look impressive to me are not necessarily the ones he will keep. Cure me of the sorter's instinct that always seems to flatter me. Make me one of the fish who is willing to be sorted and not the angel who is impatient to do the sorting.

Amen.
rewritten:
Jesus, Your parable in Matthew 13 says the kingdom is like a net drawn through the sea, gathering every kind of fish. The net is Your work. The final sorting is also Yours.

Forgive me for trying to do the angels' work early. I make judgments too quickly. I decide who belongs, who is hopeless, who is impressive, and who is beneath my concern. That is bad theology, and it has made me less merciful than You have been to me.

Give me faithfulness for the work You have actually given me: to bear witness, to love my neighbor, to repent of my own sin, and to leave final judgment in Your hands.

Cure me of the sorter's instinct when it flatters me. Make me humble enough to be gathered by grace.

Amen.
